h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֵׁנִי, מַאֲמָר א׳ Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni — Maamar Aleph

p: In Sefer Yetzirah, He crowned the letter Kuf
over sleep, and Adar in the year,
according to the version of the Geonim,
(at the beginning of chapter 5) according to the Geonim,
who counted the faculty of sleep
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּזְכָּר רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר מַאֲמָר ח)
(as was mentioned in Rosh Chodesh Adar, ma'amar 8);
and according to the version of the Arizal,
the letter Kuf is over laughter.
And certainly both these and those
are the words of the living God,
and regarding the version of the Geonim too,
that of the number one hundred
the most hidden of all hidden, through one hundred,
in the secret of the hundred blessings, etc.";
that she made of them a crown
and placed it upon the head
of the Tzaddik, Life of the Worlds,
"Blessings are upon the head of the righteous."
That is, the number one hundred indicates
when it is comprised of all the middos,
each one of them comprised of ten.
that the letter Kuf is the letter of the serpent,
who goes after the secret of the Woman of Valor,
wishing to resemble the letter Hei;
that the letter Kuf does not settle
at all in its place, etc.,
and it rules in the place of Gehinnom;
they said: Kuf stands for Kadosh.
in the holy letters of the alef-beis;
and so too it is the complete number,
and in the kelipah there is a "beginning" of the kelipah,
and it too is the letter Kuf
(as explained in Rosh Chodesh Adar, ma'amar 3;
and it is the root of the kelipah
and does not toil in Torah, etc.";
that they slackened their hands from the Torah,
and therefore Amalek came upon them."
And Amalek is the root of the yetzer hara,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קס, א)
"'Amalek, etc.' — he is the evil inclination,
the accuser who prosecutes man, etc."
And he casts slackness of hands
for he casts coldness upon a person
and laziness against toiling in Torah,
and this is the "beginning" of the kelipah.
Likewise there is a Gehinnom of fire
corresponding to desire, the serpent's enticement,
on account of matters of hinom
And there is a Gehinnom of snow
corresponding to coldness, the root of the kelipah,
who "happened upon you" and chilled you;
"And where do they complete their punishment?
the snow is their shadow of death."
And this is what they said in the holy Zohar,
that the letter Kuf rules in the place of Gehinnom,
the aspect of Kuf, as stated.
And regarding the eradication of Amalek
from all your enemies round about";
that is, when one merits to rectify
the root of the yetzer hara,
from all the accusations of the yetzer hara,
"'Even his enemies He makes at peace with him'
And as is said in the name of our master Rebbe Bunim,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing,
that the plain sense of the verse (Devarim 21:10)
"When you go out to war against your enemies"
and this is not merely by way of hint.
In truth it is all one,
and each depends on the other,
for all the dominion of the enemies
and when Hashem gives rest "from all your enemies,"
from all the accusations of the yetzer hara,
then as a matter of course "the house of Esav shall be
Now in the first utterance, "In the beginning,"
darkness, tohu and vohu are mentioned,
which alludes to the deeds of the wicked;
the night following the holy Shabbos,
and afterward by day, "Let there be light";
and "the beginning of downfall is sleep,"
"'And behold, it was very good' — this is sleep.
Is sleep then very good? etc.
Rather, because a person sleeps a little,
he rises and toils greatly in Torah."
That is, Hashem Yisbarach created the darkness
so that it should be very good,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
along the lines of what is said (Zohar II, 184a):
except that which comes forth from within darkness,
except that which comes forth from within evil."
he will rise and toil greatly in Torah,
and the light will shine forth from within the darkness.
And Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
the revelation of the attribute of Atika Kadisha,
and it is brought on this in the holy Zohar
that he "came into the supernal days."
That is, he merited to be clarified in his attribute
all the way to the root,
even in the first three sefiros;
and this is what "old" alludes to:
as is hinted in Bereishis Rabbah (58:9):
And this is the aspect of Kuf,
the secret of the hundred blessings,
דְּהַיְינוּ כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן אִיהוּ כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת
that is, Kesser Elyon is Kesser Malchus,
when it is comprised of all the middos,
And the attribute of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
קְרָא זְרִיזוּתֵיהּ דְּאַבְרָהָם קָא מַשְׁמַע לָן
"The verse is teaching us Avraham's alacrity."
Alacrity is the opposite of laziness,
so that he rises and toils
"There is none who knows how to slander like Haman."
for in that there are those who could disparage more;
and the opening of his accusation was
which is "laziness casts a deep sleep";
וְרַבָּנָן גַּם כֵּן עַם אֶחָד הֵן
and "the Rabbis too are one people with them"
slackened their hands from the Torah.
He of whom it is said, 'Hashem is One,'
is asleep, away from His people.
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to him:
Before Me there is no sleep, etc.,
yet you said there is sleep before Me —
by your life, from within sleep
I will rouse Myself against that man
and destroy him; thus it is written
'Then Hashem awoke as one asleep, etc.'"
to the point that their decree was sealed
as they said in Midrash Rabbah
presumably there was room to accuse,
for they had slackness of hands
But afterward, in that very month,
"this is Torah," as they said in the Gemara
which is called orah, a feminine term,
for then they merited Torah she'b'al peh,
"They accepted it anew in the days of Achashverosh";
for it was regarding this that there was
the holding of the mountain over them like a barrel
that he could dominate them in this month,
which was formed with the letter Kuf,
which indicates the aspect of serpent and sleep;
for they carried out the eradication of Amalek,
who is the root of the yetzer hara,
and they merited the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
that was created on the first day;
and about this it is said (Yeshayah 9:1),
And as for sleep: because he sleeps a little,
and this is "the light that comes forth, etc."
For certainly "the beginning of downfall is sleep,"
"For the righteous one falls seven times and rises,"
he comes to even greater alacrity;
and slackness of hands from the Torah,
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מַכּוֹת ז, ב)
and this is along the lines of what they said (Makkos 7b):
"a descent that is for the sake of an ascent."
as they said in the Gemara;
that is, to rectify the root of the serpent's blemish:
and the washing of the hands
alludes to the removal of self-interest;
that is, to remove the serpent's blemish
for the time in this month
is for the eradication of Amalek,
by the hand of Yosef's descendants,
he being the opposite of Esav,
as enumerated in Midrash Tanchuma (Ki Seitzei 10);
against the holiness of Klal Yisrael in this,
that he would cut off, etc.
and just as he was divided into two tribes,
so Adar is divided into two
וְכָל מִי שֶׁגּוֹדֵר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֶרְוָה
And whoever fences himself off from immorality
and then the woman was created;
the Satan was created with her"; see there.
there is the accusation of the yetzer hara
from the contamination of the serpent;
but the month was formed with the letter Kuf
so that they can rectify it,
and carry out the eradication of Amalek,
the aspect of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
who merited the aspect of Kuf,
the secret of the hundred, as mentioned above.
And this is what they said in Midrash Rabbah
"Before Me there is no sleep, etc.,"
and the faculties He created in man
for the creation of the world, as is known;
one rises and toils greatly in Torah
as though asleep, away from His people,
and sealed with a seal of clay —
for from this it came about
that Haman was destroyed from the world.
And this is what He said: "From within sleep
that on Purim they merited to grasp
and not only to accept sufferings with joy,
that it is truly for the good,
that Haman's decree brought it about
to carry out the eradication of Amalek,
and to say that this was the intent
(as explained at the fourteenth of Adar Rishon,
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן נַעֲשָׂה מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק.
and thereby the eradication of Amalek was accomplished.
And they merited Torah she'b'al peh
and this is the aspect of "the light
that comes forth from within darkness":
he rises and toils greatly in Torah.

paragraphs.text: Sefer Chachmoni, Sefer Yetzirah, chapter 5, pp. 75–76, 78 — “He made qof rule and tied a crown to it, engraving it at the beginning of speech. ... He formed with it the constellation Pisces in the world, the month Adar in the year, and the left leg in the soul. ... The opposite of sleep is wakefulness, namely being awake. ... With qof were formed Pisces, Adar, the left leg, sleep, and wakefulness.” The actual original chapter gives the full correspondence explicitly in its concluding table, and the commentary on page 78 again associates qof and the left leg with sleep and wakefulness. This independently verifies the sleep–Adar reading cited here through Sefer Chachmoni. Its wording is fuller than Rav Tzadok's compressed formula 'He made qof rule over sleep'; it should be distinguished from the laughter recension quoted elsewhere.

paragraphs.text: HaGra on Sefer Yetzirah 5:3 — “But in the writings of the Arizal he wrote laughter for Naftali and walking for Zevulun, and in place of Levi he wrote Menasheh; and it is all one, so that the tribes come in the order of the banners.” The Arizal's text is Maamar Kedishin, on the letter Kuf: “it is given to Naftali and reigns over laughter; it created ... Adar in the year.” The Geonic version that Rav Tzadok has just cited assigns Kuf to sleep. See also the note on Rosh Chodesh Adar, maamar 6.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 17:5 — “Hashem God caused a deep sleep to fall. Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in Rabbi Levi's name: The beginning of a fall is sleep: he sleeps and does not labor in Torah or do work. Rav said: There are three deep sleeps: the deep sleep of ordinary sleep, the deep sleep of prophecy, and the deep sleep of stupor.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Acharei Mos 6 — “There is a level in the kelipah called snow, and it is the first of nations … what is his Torah and service worth?… And against this there are two kinds of Gehinnom.” This shows what the cold of Amalek does. It humbles even great people until they stop learning, as Osniel ben Kenaz feared, and so its punishment is the Gehinnom of snow.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Re'eh 13 — “Chizkiyah said: The judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom is twelve months: six months in heat and six months in cold. ... Where do they complete their punishment? Rabbi Yehudah bar Rabbi says: In snow, as it is written, When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it snowed in Tzalmon. The snow is their shadow of death.” Rav Tzadok associates the cold punishment with spiritual coldness and laziness, in contrast to the fire associated with inflamed desire.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 54:1 — “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: This is the evil inclination. Ordinarily a person who grows up with his fellow for two or three years in a town binds himself to him in love. This one grows up with a person from youth to old age: if it finds him at seventy, it makes him fall; if at eighty, it makes him fall. ... Shlomo said: If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread; if he is thirsty, give him water: from the bread of Torah and the water of Torah.” The Midrash interprets the enemy in Mishlei 16:7 as the evil inclination and explains its mastery through Torah. This supports Rav Tzadok's inward reading of victory over enemies.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Seitzei 2 — “In the Zohar Chadash: ‘When you go out to war against your enemy’ — this is the yetzer hara … and then he will be given into a person's hand.” The Zohar Chadash supports Rebbe Bunim's reading. paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 9:6 — “Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said: Behold, very good—behold, sleep is good. Is sleep very good? Is it not taught that wine and sleep are fitting for the wicked and fitting for the world? Rather, because a person sleeps a little, he rises and labors greatly in Torah.” The distinction is purposeful sleep that renews Torah labor, rather than sleep as abandonment of labor.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Kometz HaMincha II 64 — “Before every ascent to a higher level there is a fall … for such is the order of creation: ‘day and night shall not cease’… but in the future… there will be no fall.” Rav Tzadok reads the night between every two days as the pattern of spiritual life. Darkness is the necessary ground of light until the yetzer is slaughtered.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 129a–b, Chayei Sarah — “Avraham drew near to Him, and this was his yearning all his days. Avraham did not draw near in one day or at one time; his deeds brought him near each day, from level to level, until he rose through his levels. When he grew old and entered the higher levels fittingly, it says, 'Avraham was old'; then he 'came into the days'—those supernal days, those days known in the mystery of faith. ... Fortunate are the masters of repentance, for in one hour, one day, one moment, they draw near to the Holy One, blessed be He, as even completely righteous people did not over many years.” The source explicitly interprets Avraham's age through entry into supernal days, reached through his life's deeds. The maamar reads that attainment as purification of his attribute up to its highest root; its discussion of renewed Torah exertion draws on the same ascent.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Rambam, Mishneh Torah, Hilchos Deos 3:3 — “He should intend that his body be sound and strong so that his soul will be properly directed to know Hashem; one cannot understand and contemplate the disciplines while hungry or ill or when one of his limbs is in pain. … Even when he is sleeping, if he deliberately sleeps so that his mind may rest and his body recover, lest he become ill and be unable to serve Hashem, his sleep itself becomes service of the Omnipresent, blessed be He. Concerning this our Sages commanded, 'Let all your actions be for the sake of Heaven.' This is what Shlomo said in his wisdom: 'In all your ways know Him, and He will straighten your paths.'”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rambam gives a practical halachic form to the conversion of sleep from downfall into service: the rest must be deliberately directed toward restoring the capacity to know and serve Hashem. It is not only the subsequent learning that acquires value; the sleep itself becomes avodah. This sharpens Rav Tzadok's statement that sleep can generate renewed alacrity and abundant Torah toil, without treating unqualified inactivity as holy.

paragraphs.text: Esther Rabbah 7:12 — “There is one people: the One of whom it is said, Hashem is One, has fallen asleep from His people. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: There is no sleep before Me, as it is written, Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps. Yet you said that there is sleep before Me! By your life, from sleep I shall awaken against that man and destroy him from the world, as it is written, Hashem awakened as one who sleeps and struck His enemies backward.” That man refers to Haman. The Midrash presents his charge of Divine sleep as the point from which the reversal will emerge.

The fall followed by waking is how teshuvah separates evil from good in this world.

paragraphs.text: Makkot 7b — “The Sages taught: Or he cast upon him includes a descent undertaken for an ascent. Rabbi Abahu asked Rabbi Yochanan: If a person was ascending a ladder and a rung slipped from beneath him, fell, and killed someone, what is the law? Is this ascent or descent? He answered: You have encountered a descent undertaken for an ascent.” The phrase belongs to the laws of accidental killing and exile. Rav Tzadok borrows it to describe a spiritual descent that becomes the means to renewed ascent.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 53b — “Rav Yehudah said in Rav's name, and it was taught likewise: You shall sanctify yourselves refers to the first washing of the hands; and you shall be holy refers to the final washing; for holy refers to oil; I am Hashem your God refers to the blessing.” The teaching expounds Vayikra 20:7. Rav Tzadok develops the first washing as the removal of the personal bias introduced through bodily desire.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 17:6 — “Rabbi Chanina son of Rav Idi said: From the beginning of the book until here the letter samech is not written. When she was created, Satan was created with her. If someone tells you, It says He is the one that surrounds, tell him: Scripture there is speaking of rivers.” The Midrash makes a textual play on the first samech in the human narrative. Rav Tzadok applies it to the moral struggle surrounding desire; it should not be converted into a claim that women themselves are evil.

p: And afterward comes the month of Nissan,
which corresponds to the tribe of Yehudah,
from whom Mashiach ben David issues,
And this is the depth of what they said
for the month of Adar corresponds to Yosef,
and afterward Nissan corresponds to Yehudah,
from whom comes Mashiach the redeemer.
And this is what they said (Taanis 29b):
let him make himself available in Adar,
Seemingly it would fit better in Nissan,
which was more of a redemption,
for regarding Adar it is brought (Megillah 14a):
that in Nissan the essence of the redemption was
to benefit Klal Yisrael and elevate them;
they would not have struck him;
and they warned him of the plagues,
and only because he rebelled did they strike him;
and when he pursued Klal Yisrael
they were drowned in the sea;
and many of the eirev rav
whom Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, accepted,
for they said that they too
would be called by the name of Yisrael.
This is not so in Adar,
to carry out the eradication of Amalek,
"but on the spoil they laid not their hand"
and they did not want at all
to extract the holy sparks from them;
and it is brought (Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 11,
that converts are not accepted from Amalek.
Therefore "let him make himself available in Adar,"
for that is the time of victory over them.
And this month, which was formed
with the letter Kuf for Kadosh,
is the time to rectify the serpent's blemish,
is the attribute of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
"They shall sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov";
for Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
and knew nothing of the serpent's counsel,
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא מֵת [תַּעֲנִית ה, ב].
and therefore he did not die (Taanis 5b).
And likewise Rebbi, every Shabbos-eve twilight,
And it is brought in Sefer Chassidim
that he would discharge his household's obligation of Kiddush;
and this is for the reason
that he knew nothing at all of bodily pleasure,
as he said, "It is revealed and known, etc.,
and I did not derive benefit
and therefore he did not die,
like Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him
and he was called Rabbeinu HaKadosh
is the aspect of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
and he was a spark of his soul,
as is cited from the holy Arizal.
וְדָא הוּא רָזָא דְּאוֹת וָאו כּוּלֵּי
and this is the secret of the letter Vav, etc.,"
as they said in the holy Zohar
For through the holiness of Yosef
the root of the serpent's blemish,
to be as before the blemish;
and this is the root of the work of the month of Adar,
which was formed with the letter Kuf
and given to Yosef, as mentioned above.
And this is what they said (Rosh Hashanah 29a):
along the lines of what they said (Berachos 33a):
"It is not the arod that kills;
rather it is sin that kills."
is the root of the yetzer hara,
which brought desire into the heart,
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּרָזָא דְּאָת ק׳
and it too is in the secret of the letter Kuf,
and it too is the "beginning" of the kelipah;
and when they subjugate their hearts
"he would look at the copper serpent and live"
along the lines of what is said in the holy Zohar:
except that which comes forth from within darkness."
And one can bring desire into holiness,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קלז, א)
that in the future it will not be repulsive
and immerses himself from his impurity;
for were it not for it,
the joy of Torah study would not exist
And the opening of the Mishnah
"'And it was, when Moshe raised his hand,
And it has no connection to that place,
except for what was written by
since it is dealing with intention of the heart,
that at the time they direct their hearts to Heaven.
And this is what we learned (ibid. 27b):
"And he heard the sound of the shofar
or the sound of the Megillah —
if he directed his heart, he has fulfilled his obligation, etc.,
And this needs to be understood:
the law of intention of the heart
at the beginning of the second chapter of Berachos (13a),
and there he should have taught
of "And it was, when he raised, etc."
But according to what has been said,
it fits well: the reading of the Megillah
who "happened upon you" and chilled you,
and slackness of hands from the Torah —
Likewise the matter of the shofar on Rosh Hashanah:
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא גְּזֵרַת הַכָּתוּב
although it is a decree of Scripture,
there is a hint in it:
and you slumberers, rouse yourselves from your slumber"
פֶּרֶק ג מֵהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה הֲלָכָה ד).
And on this he then brought
that when they directed their hearts to Heaven
Corresponding to the Megillah he brought
"And it was, when Moshe raised his hand,
corresponding to the sound of the shofar,
"he would look at the copper serpent and live,"
that one can find life in this;
this was created to serve man
for the service of Hashem Yisbarach,
which is that he should have
for were it not for the yetzer hara,
the joy of Torah study would not exist,
as they said in the holy Zohar.
And this is what is brought (Sukkah 52b),
expounding "He who pampers his servant from youth"
as referring to the yetzer hara,
which was created to be a servant to man,
for this was the purpose of man's creation:
And the serpent, in the literal sense,
was meant to be a great attendant to assist him
the yetzer of desire will not be abolished;
rather the yearning for Torah will remain,
And it is brought from our master Rabbi Chaim Vital, of blessed memory
that nachash has the numerical value of Mashiach;
וְזֶהוּ וְהִבִּיט אֶל נְחַשׁ נְחֹשֶׁת וָחָי
and this is "he would look at the copper serpent and live":
that he take eternal life from it,
And regarding the shofar we find in the Yerushalmi
"And when he hears it a second time,
he says: Surely this is the shofar
of 'a great shofar shall be sounded,' etc."
even the heart of "those lost in the land of Ashur
and those cast away in the land of Egypt";
that is, even though they are sunk
so that their sins become like merits —
the light that comes forth from within darkness.
And this is the work of this month:
to rectify things so that sleep
is only in order to come to alacrity,
"The night was created only for sleep"
"The moon was created only for study."
That is, the attribute of night
the moon that receives from the sun,
"For Hashem is a sun and a shield";
"And when He would teach him the Oral Law,
he knew that it was night, etc."
And it uses the term "for girsa,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט, א)
along the lines of what they said (Avodah Zarah 19a):
"A person should keep reciting his learning,
he does not know what he is saying."
And this alludes to good sleep:
that because he sleeps a little,
he rises and toils greatly in Torah;
and the toil is from the side of man,
But to merit illumination in the heart,
as we say (in the blessing Ahavas Olam),
"And illuminate our eyes in Your Torah" —
this is only from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
And about this they said (Eruvin ibid.):
he said to them, "They are from the daytime."
And this is what they said:
"The moon was created only for study,"
for this is from the side of man.
there is the aspect of dreaming,
and Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
And we said that the crown of kingship
that Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him, merited —
is the light of Torah she'b'al peh
that Hashem Yisbarach gives as a gift,
and it is the wealth of knowledge
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
while the Menorah, which is also
the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh —
is what a person merits through his toil,
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים
and it too is the words of the living God;
he rises and toils greatly in Torah.
And this is the main work of this month:
to rectify the blemish of the yetzer hara and the serpent,
which casts coldness and laziness upon a person —
And by rectifying it, one merits
and this too is in the secret of the hundred.
And this is the eradication of Amalek:
and the desire through which he cast contamination;
וְעַל זֶה נוֹצַר בְּאוֹת ק׳ קָדוֹשׁ
and therefore it was formed with the letter Kuf for Kadosh:
the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
the light that comes forth from within darkness;
Hashem is a light for me."

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 11 — “It was taught in Rabbi Ilai's name: The Holy One, blessed be He, swore: My right hand, My right hand; My throne, My throne! If converts come from all the nations of the world, I accept them; but the offspring of Amalek I do not accept forever.” This is the Midrashic teaching Rav Tzadok cites in his distinction between extracting holy sparks from Egypt and the eradication of Amalek. It is presented here as a source for his discourse, not as a practical determination of anyone's ancestry or conversion status.

paragraphs.text: Taanit 5b — “Rabbi Yochanan said: Our father Yaakov did not die. They asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed, and the buriers buried him? He answered: I am expounding a verse: Do not fear, My servant Yaakov ... for I shall save you from afar and your offspring from the land of their captivity. It compares him to his offspring: just as his offspring are alive, so he is alive.”

paragraphs.text: Ketubot 103a — “Let the lamp be lit in its place, the table set in its place, and the bed spread in its place. Why? Every Friday evening he would come to his house.” The passage follows Rabbi's instructions before his death and describes his continued Friday-evening presence in the home.

paragraphs.text: Sefer Chassidim 1129 — “Our holy master would appear in the fine garments that he wore on Shabbos, not in shrouds, to show that he remained in his full strength. He discharged the obligation of the many in the sanctification of the day, unlike other dead people who are free from the commandments: he was as a living person in the clothes he wore in his life. The righteous are called living even in death, and he discharged his household's obligation in Kiddush.” This is the explicit source for Kiddush, a detail not stated in the quoted sentence from Kesubos 103a.

paragraphs.text: Ketubot 104a — “As Rabbi was dying, he raised his ten fingers upward and said: Master of the world, it is revealed and known before You that I labored in Torah with my ten fingers and did not take pleasure even with my little finger. May it be Your will that there be peace in my rest. A heavenly voice went forth and said: Let peace come; they shall rest on their beds.”

paragraphs.text: Likkutei HaShas of the Ari, Avos 2:1 — “Rabbi says, 'Whatever brings honor to the one who does it,' etc. Know that Rabbeinu HaKadosh is Yaakov Avinu himself. This is the meaning of 'whatever brings honor to the one who does it.' Understand this.” The original Lurianic passage identifies Rebbi with Yaakov directly. Its immediate context is Rebbi's teaching about tiferes, the attribute associated with Yaakov; Rav Tzadok invokes the soul connection in explaining their shared holiness.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 29a — “Similarly it says: Make yourself a fiery serpent and place it on a pole; anyone bitten shall see it and live. Does a serpent kill or give life? Rather, when Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they were healed; otherwise they wasted away.” The Mishnah places this immediately after the teaching about Moshe's raised hands in the war with Amalek. Rav Tzadok explains both through direction of the heart.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 33a — “Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa took the dead arvad on his shoulder and brought it to the study hall. He told them: See, my children: the arvad does not kill; sin kills. At that time they said: Woe to the person met by an arvad, and woe to the arvad met by Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa.” Arvad is the dangerous creature described in the preceding narrative. Rav Tzadok invokes the episode to identify the moral root beneath the serpent image.

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 3:4 — “Although sounding the shofar on Rosh HaShanah is a decree of Scripture, it contains a hint: Awaken, sleepers, from your sleep; slumberers, arise from your slumber. Examine your deeds, return in repentance, and remember your Creator. Those who forget truth in the vanities of time and spend their whole year in emptiness and nothingness that neither benefits nor saves: look to your souls and improve your ways and deeds.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 4 — “The yetzer hara was created for good; only man spoils it and makes it evil. … desire: ‘Were it not for the yetzer hara, the joy of learning would not exist.’” Rav Tzadok extends the point beyond desire. Each root of the yetzer, envy and honor as well, has its holy use in the service of Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52b — “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonasan's name: The evil inclination incites a person in this world and testifies against him in the World to Come, as it is said, One who pampers his servant from youth will in the end have him as a manon. In Rabbi Chiyya's atbach cipher, a witness is called manon.” The Gemara identifies the servant with the evil inclination. Rav Tzadok develops the image further: the inclination was created to serve the person's Torah and Divine service.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 59b — “Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says: Alas for the great attendant lost from the world! Had the serpent not been cursed, each Jew would have had two good serpents: he could send one north and one south to bring fine precious stones and pearls. Moreover, he could sling a strap beneath its tail, and it would carry earth for his garden and ruin.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 12 — “Of the kelipah of desire something will remain in the future too… and the yearning for Torah will remain from it … for the meaning of yetzer is desire, as in ‘l'yetzer machshevos levav.’” Rav Tzadok grounds the claim in the word itself. Yetzer means desire, and that desire, once cleansed, is the holiness Yisrael drew out of Mitzrayim.

paragraphs.text: Sefer HaLikkutim, Shoftim, s.v. U'mah Shekasuv Ve'Inakmah (Jerusalem 5748, p. 364) — “Regarding 'Let me exact vengeance for one of my two eyes': these are aspects of Netzach and Hod, which become hair. Since he had damaged them, he now wished to repair them through his death, and he put the external forces to death with him, since he had supplied them with a flow of holiness and vitality by joining with them. ... When our father Yaakov saw this, he said, 'For Your salvation I hope, Hashem'—not through this one, whom I had thought to be Mashiach; he has turned into nachash, for they have the same numerical value.” The passage concerns Shimshon and explicitly supplies the equality of nachash and Mashiach. Its account moves from failed messianic promise to the serpent; Rav Tzadok develops the possibility of taking eternal life from the serpent through repentance and turning the heart toward Heaven.

paragraphs.text: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 16b, s.v. Kedei learbev — “The Aruch explains, as in the Yerushalmi: It is written, He shall swallow death forever, and On that day a great shofar shall be sounded. When he hears the shofar once, he is alarmed but not fully alarmed. When he hears it a second time, he says: Surely this is the shofar that shall be sounded as the great shofar, and my time has come to be swallowed up. He becomes confused and has no time to prosecute.” This verifies the teaching through Tosafos quoting the Aruch in the Yerushalmi's name, the intermediary identified in Rav Tzadok's citation. It is not presented as an independently located passage in the extant Yerushalmi.

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 65a — “Rav Yehudah said: Night was created only for sleep. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Moonlight was created only for study. They told Rabbi Zeira: Your teachings are sharp. He answered: They belong to the daytime.” The juxtaposition allows Rav Tzadok to distinguish restorative sleep and nighttime review from the clarity bestowed in the light of day.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 36 — “How did Moshe know when it was day? When the Holy One, blessed be He, taught him Written Torah, he knew it was day. When He taught him orally, Mishnah and Talmud, he knew it was night. For day and night are alike before the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, Light dwells with Him; and Even darkness does not darken for You; night shines like day, darkness is like light.”

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 19a — “Rava said: A person should always review, even though he forgets and even though he does not know what he is saying, as it is written, My soul breaks for longing. It is written breaks, not grinds.” Rav Tzadok reads review as the person's necessary effort even before he receives clear inward understanding.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, The Fifteenth of Av 5 — “Night, the aspect of the moon that receives from the sun … of reasoning they said, ‘Your teachings are sharp — they are from the daytime.’” This identifies the night's work as review, the human labor of keeping the Oral Torah. For that reason learning at night is added from the fifteenth of Av, and “there is no song of Torah except at night.”
